summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, neurogenic bladder with chronic indwelling Foley catheter, paraplegia, and polysubstance abuse was readmitted for pyelonephritis after leaving the hospital against medical advice one day prior during a previous admission. She presented with severe left flank pain, fever, and chills, and was found to have a multidrug-resistant urinary tract infection caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus species. She was treated with a full 14-day course of IV meropenem and linezolid, despite a two-day interruption in therapy due to PICC line failure. Her kidney function transiently worsened with mild acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia, both of which resolved with IV fluids. A pruritic rash developed during admission and was treated with hydrocortisone cream. A blocked tear duct was managed with erythromycin ointment and warm compresses. Pain was controlled with acetaminophen and limited oral dilaudid. The Foley catheter was changed before discharge. She completed treatment, was afebrile and stable, and was discharged home with instructions to monitor for infection recurrence and maintain catheter hygiene.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
